summary.overall: Left/right handedness is consistent: LH/driver is +z. Every system is on the correct side and end of the car, and the intake/exhaust orientation is correct. The main problem is systematic: the renderer treats cyl size[0] as the radius, but most rotating parts were sized as if it were the diameter. That makes rotors, drums, the clutch, alternator, water pump, A/C compressor, fan, starter, pipes and hoses 2–3× too big, and it causes the pile-up at the passenger belt end. The wheel/hub stack sits 0.2–0.46 below the shell's wheel center (1.44), and both belts and the spark-plug row are rotated 90°. The mid pipe also runs through the fuel tank.

lh_evidence: All LH-named parts sit at +z: fender-l, door-fl, door-rl, strut-fl, cv-axle-l (driver), headlamp-l, taillamp-l, wheel-fl and wheel-rl. All RH-named parts sit at -z. The driver seat, steering column, ignition switch, key, battery, airbox, PCM, CJB and transaxle are at +z. The passenger seat, degas bottle, blower, cabin filter, timing belt, serpentine belt, alternator, PS pump and A/C compressor are at -z. The sides are consistent everywhere, with intake toward the firewall (x 4.5) and exhaust toward the radiator (x 6.9).

findings.problem: The wheel center is at y 0.98 with radius 1.3, so the tire sinks 0.32 below ground. The shell wheel profile puts the front wheel center at cy 1.439, r 1.439 (rear cy 1.393), so this part is 0.46 low and sits inside the arch. The same applies to wheel-fr, wheel-rl and wheel-rr (rear y 1.39).
findings.why: A wheel's center sits one tire radius above the ground and has to match the shell's wheel arch.

findings.problem: The hub, rotor and CV axles are at y 1.24, but the wheel center is 1.44. The whole corner stack is 0.2 low and not on the axle line. The same applies to rotor-f, caliper-f/pads-f (+0.2), cv-axle-l and cv-axle-r (y 1.44), and wheel-brg-r, drum-r and shoes-r (y 1.39).
findings.why: The hub, rotor, CV outer joint and wheel all share one spin axis.

findings.problem: size[0] is the radius (CylinderGeometry(r,r,len)), so r 0.95 means a 1.9-unit (about 46 cm) disc. A 258 mm rotor at about 0.244 m/unit is r 0.53. The rotor also nearly fills the wheel.
findings.why: The Mk1 Focus front rotor is 258 mm diameter, inside a 15-inch wheel.

findings.problem: r 0.8 gives a drum about 39 cm across. A 203 mm drum is r 0.42.
findings.why: The rear drum is 203 mm diameter and about 50 mm wide.

findings.problem: r 1.1 gives a clutch disc about 54 cm across, larger than the engine block is tall. The real disc is about 220 mm, so r 0.45.
findings.why: The Zetec/MTX-75 clutch is about 220 mm diameter.

findings.problem: r 0.75 gives an alternator about 37 cm across (the real one is about 13 cm). It also overlaps the block, the water pump, the A/C compressor and the 2.4-wide exhaust manifold at the passenger end.
findings.why: The Zetec Focus alternator is a compact unit about 130 mm across, low on the front (exhaust) face at the belt end. Suggested pos: [7.0,1.9,-1.15].

findings.problem: r 0.65 gives about 32 cm across. It is also centered at x 6.4, which is inside the block (x 4.77–6.67).
findings.why: The compressor bolts low on the front face of the block at the belt end. Also resize to [0.28,0.55].

findings.problem: The box is [0.3,2.6,2.2], so it is thin in x and runs 2.2 along z, the crank axis. The belt plane should be perpendicular to the crank (x-y plane). As modeled it cuts through the block from z -2.6 to -0.4.
findings.why: On a transverse engine the timing belt runs in a fore/aft-vertical plane at the passenger end. Use pos z -1.4.

findings.problem: Same orientation error as timing-belt: [0.25,2.6,2.2] runs along the crank axis and goes through the block.
findings.why: The accessory belt sits outboard of the timing cover, in a plane perpendicular to the crank. Use pos z -1.7.

findings.problem: The plug/coil row is 2.4 long in x (fore/aft), but the cylinders are in line along z on a transverse engine.
findings.why: The four plugs run along the head centerline, parallel to the crankshaft.

findings.problem: At z -1.6 with r 0.3, the pipe spans z -1.9 to -1.3 and y 0.2 to 0.8, so it passes through the fuel tank (z ±1.5, y 0.5–1.4). r 0.3 is also a 15 cm pipe; the real one is about 5 cm.
findings.why: The exhaust routes beside the tank, never through it. Also resize to [0.1,7.2].

findings.problem: r 0.25 gives a pipe about 12 cm across; the real front pipe is about 5 cm.
findings.why: The front pipe on the 2.0 Zetec is about 50 mm OD.

findings.problem: [1,1.8,2.4] covers the whole front face of the block, end to end. It swallows the alternator, O2 sensor and A/C region, and reaches x 7.4, nearly touching the fan.
findings.why: The 4-into-1 manifold and close-coupled cat are about 40 cm wide, centered on the ports. Use pos [7.0,2.2,0.2].

findings.problem: r 0.7 gives about 34 cm across (the real one is about 10 cm), and it overlaps the alternator and the block.
findings.why: The Zetec water pump is a small belt-driven unit at the passenger end of the block. Suggested pos: [6.75,2.45,-1.2].

findings.problem: At [5.4,3,-1.8] with r 0.5, it overlaps strut-fr (x 5.1–5.7, z -2.6 to -2.0), motor-mounts and the belts.
findings.why: On the Zetec Focus the PS pump sits on the rear (intake) side at the belt end. Also resize to [0.3,0.6].

findings.problem: At [5.7,3.2,-2.2] the 0.8 cube overlaps strut-fr and the coolant degas bottle, so three parts share the same space.
findings.why: The RH engine mount bolts to the top of the timing-end bracket, just ahead of and inboard of the strut tower.

findings.problem: It overlaps motor-mounts (x 5.75–6.1, z -2.6 to -2.15).
findings.why: The degas bottle sits on the RH inner fender, ahead of the strut tower.

findings.problem: r 1.1 gives a fan 2.2 across, taller than the radiator (1.6), so it sticks out above and below the core.
findings.why: The fan shroud fits within the radiator core, about 38 cm fan.

findings.problem: [0.45,0.9] gives a filter about 22 cm across and 22 cm long. The FL-400S is about 76 × 100 mm.
findings.why: The FL-400S is a small spin-on filter.

findings.problem: r 0.55 gives about 27 cm across; the real starter is about 9 cm.
findings.why: The Focus starter is a compact gear-reduction unit on the rear of the bellhousing.

findings.problem: r 0.6 gives about 29 cm across; the real bore is about 55 mm.
findings.why: The Zetec throttle body is about 60 mm bore.

findings.problem: r 0.25 gives a hose about 12 cm across; the real hose is about 3.5 cm.
findings.why: Radiator hoses are about 32–38 mm ID.

findings.problem: r 0.7 gives about 34 cm across.
findings.why: The blower wheel is about 15 cm across.

findings.problem: [0.3,1.6,1.8] is about 39 × 44 cm, far too big. Its ex [0,5,0] is the same as dash, so it never separates from it when exploded.
findings.why: The heater core is about 15 × 25 cm. Also give it ex [-1,4,-3] so it clears the dash.

findings.problem: At x -2.4, z 1.2 it is inside the fuel tank volume (x -4.1 to -1.5, z ±1.5).
findings.why: The in-line filter mounts on the underbody rail ahead of the tank, not inside it.

findings.problem: 2.6 × 0.9 × 3.0 units is about 63 × 22 × 73 cm, roughly 100 L, which is double 13.2 gal (50 L).
findings.why: The Mk1 Focus tank holds 50 L.

findings.problem: The strut bottom (y 1.8) at z 2.0–2.6 goes into the transaxle top (y ≤2.9, z ≤2.4). It is also inboard of the hub (z 2.75) instead of above the knuckle. The same applies to strut-fr on the passenger side.
findings.why: The strut lower end clamps the knuckle just inboard of the wheel, outboard of the gearbox.

findings.problem: 0.9 × 0.9 × 0.5 is about 22 cm, oversized. Once the rotor is shrunk to r 0.53 it also floats off the disc.
findings.why: A single-piston floating caliper is about 15 cm, sitting on the rotor's trailing edge. Use pos [5.9,1.8,2.55] after the y fix.

findings.problem: It sits inside the airbox volume (x 5.2–6.6).
findings.why: The MAF sits in the duct between the airbox outlet and the throttle body.

findings.problem: y 3.0 ± 0.8 is sedan height. The wagon lamps are tall units on the D-pillar. The same applies to taillamp-r.
findings.why: Focus wagon tail lamps run vertically up the D-pillar beside the liftgate. Also resize to [0.5,2.2,0.8].
